title: Session screens show the device without sessionsClient()
detail: The list, my-sessions and detail screens showed [object Object] in the device column for apps that do not register sessionsClient(). The session queries (user-session:list, user-session:mine, user-session:detail) now return a deviceLabel string such as "Chrome 141 · macOS" next to the unchanged device object, null when the user agent is unknown, and the screens render that field. sessionsClient() only adds the translated "Unknown device" for rows without a label.

title: Sessions tests no longer write projection tables directly
detail: The sessions integration tests change tenant memberships and user status through the update-member-roles handler or the event-store executor instead of writing into the projection tables. Nothing changes for apps; the package is only republished.

title: isPrincipalBlocked is no longer exported from sessions
detail: The sessions export dropped its re-export of isPrincipalBlocked, which ignored isDeleted. isPrincipalRowBlocked from the user export covers status and isDeleted and is what the session callbacks use.
migration: import isPrincipalRowBlocked (for a user row) or isPrincipalBlocked (for a bare status) from "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/user" instead of the sessions export

title: Session lists show the device
detail: The new subpath @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/sessions/web exports sessionsClient(). Apps must add sessionsClient() to their client features to get the device column (browser and OS parsed from the user agent) and the translated "This session" cell; without it the screens fall back to the raw columns. The IP display is unchanged.

title: sessionChecker looks up the user and the membership concurrently
detail: The session check starts the user lookup together with the session read and the membership lookup together with the last-seen refresh. Results and the fail-open behavior are unchanged; a failed lookup that is not needed no longer raises an unhandled rejection.

title: Session revoke (single, mass, all-others) and its revoked-event commit atomically
detail: Session logout, password-change/MFA mass revoke, revoke-all-others and PAT revoke now commit the revoke and its revoked-event in one transaction, so a failed append no longer leaves a revoked token whose SSE streams stay open. GDPR delete hooks now try every row of the subject and report all failures at once instead of stopping at the first. The notes mention-forget hook loads the mentioned notes with one query and resolves each host entity's retention policy once.

title: Session list loads one max-size page and renders no pager
store_user_sessions gets an index on (tenant_id, last_seen_at) (fw#3396)
detail: Active-user dashboard aggregates (metrics feature) filter on tenant_id and last_seen_at.
migration: Run `kumiko migrate generate` and apply the migration: it adds an index on `store_user_sessions (tenant_id, last_seen_at)`.

title: sessions:query:user-session:mine returns the paged envelope { rows, nextCursor }; new self-service my-sessions screen (fw#2844).
detail: The query backs the new `my-sessions` projectionList (open to every signed-in user): the caller's live sessions with a per-row revoke (hidden on the current session) and "sign out all other devices". Exported id SESSION_MINE_SCREEN_ID. Server-side scoping to the caller is unchanged.
migration: Breaking for direct callers of `sessions:query:user-session:mine`: read `data.rows` instead of treating `data` as the array (`nextCursor` is always null). Account-security custom screens built on this query can be replaced by a dashboard with `kind: "screen"` panels on `sessions:screen:my-sessions` and the auth-mfa screens (money-horse#477, publicstatus#435, kumiko-studio#283).

title: Session rows track lastSeenAt, refreshed hourly
detail: userSession now carries a lastSeenAt timestamp, set on session creation and refreshed by sessionChecker at most once per hour (LAST_SEEN_REFRESH_MS). A refresh failure is swallowed and the check still returns "live" — this is a coarse activity marker, not a per-request write.

title: Mid-stream access revocation aborts idle SSE pulls; sseHeartbeatMs is a real buildServer option (fw#1587).
detail: A revoked session used to keep an idle SSE stream alive until the client disconnected. clientIpOf now falls back to x-real-ip before the shared "unknown" bucket, so per-IP rate limits stop collapsing into one bucket behind proxies that only set that header.

title: Revoke handlers emit session-revoked event
detail: Session revocation now appends a session-revoked event to the aggregate stream — other features can react to it (e.g. cache invalidation).
